applicableAreas: southern property boundary, mitigation tree locations within overhead electric distribution line zone
findings.comment: Four mitigation trees are positioned 0 to 3 lateral feet from the overhead electric distribution line, placing them within the < 15 feet zone where only utility-compatible (UC) trees are permitted. However, the landscape plan does not identify the specific species of these trees or their utility-compatible status. The plan labels these features only as generic "M" (mitigation) symbols without cross-referencing species to the plant schedule. Utility-compatibility designation from ECM Appendix F cannot be verified from the landscape plan documentation alone.

applicableAreas: southern property boundary, mitigation tree locations within distribution conductor zone
findings.comment: Four mitigation trees are positioned 0 to 3 lateral feet from the overhead electric distribution line, placing them within the < 25 feet zone where large trees (40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) are prohibited. However, the landscape plan does not provide mature height information for these trees. Only installation minimum heights are specified on the plant schedule (16' minimum for shade trees). The specific species and mature heights cannot be verified from the landscape plan locations.

applicableAreas: southern property boundary and pull box locations throughout site
findings.comment: Underground electric lines, pull boxes, and potentially other underground equipment are shown on the electrical plan and near the landscape mitigation trees along the southern boundary. Trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment require minimum 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from the equipment. The landscape plan does not include root barrier details or specifications for trees near the underground utilities, and the distances to underground equipment cannot be verified from the available documentation.

Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) are not differentiated on the landscape plan. All proposed trees are identified only with generic categorical symbols (SY for street yard, PL for parking lot, M for mitigation) and generic circular tree symbols. There is no visual or textual differentiation indicating which trees are 40+ feet at maturity, making it impossible to verify clearances for large trees from overhead electric facilities. Proposed species include Live Oak and Cedar Elm, both of which typically exceed 40 feet mature height, requiring special clearance verification if planted near electric lines.

applicableAreas: southern property boundary, southeast of site near buildings 6 and 7
findings.comment: Four mitigation trees are shown on the landscape plan positioned 0 to 3 lateral feet from the overhead electric distribution conductor along the southern property boundary. These distances place the trees within the prohibited < 15 feet clearance zone established by UCM § 1.10.10.4 for distribution facilities. Overhead distribution line clearances require either documentation of utility-compatible species designation, explicit mature height limitation, or documented written approval from Austin Energy for any exceptions. No such documentation (UC designation, mature height specifications, or Austin Energy approval letter) is provided on the site plans or in supplementary project documents reviewed.
